q-54152.name: Question 1
q-54152.problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x=\frac{1}{{t}^{3}},\,y=\frac{3}{t}.$ Given that $\frac{dy}{dx}={t}^{2},$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$
q-54152.worked_solution:
To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $\frac{dy}{dx}={t}^{2},$ and we can calculate $\frac{dx}{dt}$ as follows:

$$
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{1}{{t}^{3}})=-\frac{3}{{t}^{4}}
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}({t}^{2})}{(-\frac{3}{{t}^{4}})} \\  & =\frac{2t}{(-\frac{3}{{t}^{4}})} \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}{t}^{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

A curve is defined by the parametric equations x=1t3,y=3t. Given that dydx=t2, calculate d2ydx2.

a
−23t5
b
−3t2
c
−2t3
d
2t
e
2t5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

d2ydx2=ddt(dydx)(dxdt).

We're given that dydx=t2, and we can calculate dxdt as follows:

dxdt=ddt(1t3)=−3t4

Substituting into the formula, we get

d2ydx2=ddt(t2)(−3t4)=2t(−3t4)=−23t5.

q-50323.name: Question 2
q-50323.problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t),\,y=-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2.$ Given that $\frac{dy}{dx}=2\operatorname{tan}⁡(3t),$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$
q-50323.worked_solution:
To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $\frac{dy}{dx}=2\operatorname{tan}⁡(3t),$ and we can calculate $\frac{dx}{dt}$ as follows:

$$
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t))=3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(2\operatorname{tan}⁡(3t))}{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)} \\  & =\frac{6{sec}^{2}⁡(3t)}{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)} \\  & =2{sec}^{3}⁡(3t).\end{aligned}
$$

q-122881.name: Question 3
q-122881.problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x=5\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,y=-15\operatorname{cos}⁡t.$ Given that  $\frac{dy}{dx}=3\operatorname{tan}⁡t,$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$
q-122881.worked_solution:
To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $\frac{dy}{dx}=3\operatorname{tan}⁡t,$ and we can calculate $\frac{dx}{dt}$ as follows:

$$
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}(5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=5\operatorname{cos}⁡t
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(3\operatorname{tan}⁡t)}{5\operatorname{cos}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{3{sec}^{2}⁡t}{5\operatorname{cos}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}{sec}^{3}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

A curve is defined by the parametric equations x=5sin⁡t,y=−15cos⁡t. Given that dydx=3tan⁡t, calculate d2ydx2.

a
35sec3⁡t
b
15sec5⁡t
c
13sec⁡(3t)
d
15sec2⁡t
e
35sec⁡t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

d2ydx2=ddt(dydx)(dxdt).

We're given that dydx=3tan⁡t, and we can calculate dxdt as follows:

dxdt=ddt(5sin⁡t)=5cos⁡t

Substituting into the formula, we get

d2ydx2=ddt(3tan⁡t)5cos⁡t=3sec2⁡t5cos⁡t=35sec3⁡t.

q-54160.name: Question 4
q-54160.problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x={e}^{t}-3,\,y={e}^{3t}-{e}^{t}.$ Given that  $\frac{dy}{dx}=3{e}^{2t}-1,$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$
q-54160.worked_solution:
To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $\frac{dy}{dx}=3{e}^{2t}-1,$ and we can calculate $\frac{dx}{dt}$ as follows:

$$
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}({e}^{t}-3)={e}^{t}
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(3{e}^{2t}-1)}{{e}^{t}} \\  & =\frac{6{e}^{2t}}{{e}^{t}} \\  & =6{e}^{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-122888.name: Question 5
q-122888.problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x=-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)-10,\,y=6\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)+15.$ Calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$
q-122888.worked_solution:
To find the first derivative, we will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=8\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t),\,{y}^{′}(t)=24\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t).
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{24\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)}{8\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)}=3\operatorname{cot}⁡(4t).
$$

To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(3\operatorname{cot}⁡(4t))}{8\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)} \\  & =-\frac{12{csc}^{2}⁡(4t)}{8\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}{csc}^{3}⁡(4t).\end{aligned}
$$

a
12csc3⁡(2t)
b
−32csc3⁡(4t)
c
−23csc2⁡(4t)
d
−3csc3⁡t
e
13csc⁡(3t)

To find the first derivative, we will use the formula

dydx=y′(t)x′(t).

Differentiating x and y, we get

x′(t)=8sin⁡(4t),y′(t)=24cos⁡(4t).

Therefore, dydx=24cos⁡(4t)8sin⁡(4t)=3cot⁡(4t).

To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

d2ydx2=ddt(dydx)(dxdt).

Substituting into the formula, we get

d2ydx2=ddt(3cot⁡(4t))8sin⁡(4t)=−12csc2⁡(4t)8sin⁡(4t)=−32csc3⁡(4t).

q-54156.problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x=\frac{{t}^{3}}{3},\,y={t}^{5}+2{t}^{3}$ where $t$ is a real number. Calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$
q-54156.worked_solution:
To find the first derivative, we will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)={t}^{2},\,{y}^{′}(t)=5{t}^{4}+6{t}^{2}.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{5{t}^{4}+6{t}^{2}}{{t}^{2}}=5{t}^{2}+6.
$$

To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(5{t}^{2}+6)}{{t}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{10t}{{t}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{10}{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Finally, we evaluate at $t=\frac{\pi }{4},$ and we get

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}\,{|}_{t\,=\,\frac{\pi }{4}}=-\frac{1}{4}{csc}^{3}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})=-\frac{1}{4}.
